clue.text: Odd characters might snore when it's stifling

indicators.note: the letters of the next words are treated as oddly arranged characters to be reshuffled

explanation.surface: A loud snorer makes a stuffy room feel even more airless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd characters' tells you to rearrange the letters of MIGHT SNORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Smothering and stifling both mean suffocating or stopping someone breathing.

clue.text: Near average

explanation.surface: Close to the mean.
explanation.definitionFit: Near is tight-fisted, i.e. stingy, and the mean is an arithmetic average.

clue.text: Row about a couple of pounds found in a boat

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
L is the abbreviation for pound, so two of them give LL

explanation.surface: A rower finds a few quid aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' tempts as rowing but means a tier.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiller is the bar used for steering, part of a small vessel.

clue.text: Cancelling a singer's engagement

indicators.note: engagement suggests the letters are thrown into a fight and rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A vocalist's booking has been called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engagement' signals rearranging A SINGER; the 's is not counted.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasing deletes or wipes out, which is to annul.

clue.text: Some trite magazine article

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dull piece in a periodical.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a news report or piece in a paper.

clue.text: Gained ground in Scandinavia

parts.note: got means gained
land is ground

explanation.surface: Territory was won in the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: this is a large Swedish island in the Baltic.
explanation.definitionFit: Gotland is a Baltic island belonging to Sweden, part of the Nordic region.

clue.text: Thinking to show spirit, invite a deviant

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic spirit

indicators.note: deviant says the letters stray from their order

explanation.surface: Offering a drink to a rogue to show courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' looks like courage but is RUM; 'deviant' rearranges INVITE A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruminative means pondering or meditative.

clue.text: Being fed-up with one, people start threatening vandalism

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: the word appears as written
an ace is a one in cards
men are people

indicators.note: start picks the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Fed-up youths with an attitude start threatening damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses FED to DEF; ACE is one, MEN people, T the first letter of 'threatening'.
explanation.definitionFit: Defacement is spoiling the look of something, a typical act of vandals.

clue.text: To reduce by a quarter would be shrewd

parts.note: to cut is to reduce
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A cost-cutting idea: trimming a quarter off would be the clever move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A quarter' looks like a fraction to cut away, but it is E, one of the compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A cute person can mean a sharp, clever one, a sense close to astute.

clue.text: Family man holding back letters for politicians

indicators.note: holding means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: a parent is a family man

indicators.note: back says the word for letters is turned round

parts.note: letters delivered by the post are mail

explanation.surface: A father of the household withholds some post addressed to MPs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family man' reads as the definition, but the politicians are at the end; 'back' signals the turnaround of the post.
explanation.definitionFit: The national assembly is the body made up of elected lawmakers.

clue.text: Plate obtained by the French speaking flier

parts.note: la is the feminine form of 'the' in French

indicators.note: speaking says the bird's name is given as it sounds, not as it is spelt

parts.note: a mynah is a bird, a flier

explanation.surface: Someone acquires a dish from a French-speaking airman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' suggests a pilot but is a bird, the mynah, which sounds like MINA.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamina is a thin layer or sheet, as in a metal plate.

clue.text: Trial of the guy taking a piece of jewellery

parts.note: he refers to a man, the guy
a ring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: A man is tried in court for stealing a jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' just joins HE to A RING.
explanation.definitionFit: A court hearing is a judicial trial or examination of a case.

clue.text: Simple-minded individuals

parts.note: a simple is an old word for a medicinal plant, so these are people whose minds are on such plants

explanation.definitionFit: Herbalists study and use simples, the old name for medicinal plants.

clue.text: Discharge a sailor and answer for it

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
a solution is an answer

explanation.surface: A seaman is released and must account for it.
explanation.walkthrough: AB is an able-bodied seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolution is release from guilt or sin, a formal discharge.

clue.text: A note on mature grouse

parts.note: G is a musical note
ripe means mature

explanation.surface: A musical note on a mature game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' looks like the bird but means a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A gripe is a complaint, and to grouse is to grumble.

clue.text: One doesn't feel obliged to see the ruins of Tangier

indicators.note: ruins suggests the letters of the city name have been wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A tourist goes to see the ancient remains of a Moroccan port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ruins of' signals rearranging TANGIER.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungrateful person feels no gratitude or obligation for kindness received.

clue.text: Private hotel royalty used

parts.note: an inn is a hotel
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for royalty

explanation.surface: A private hotel patronised by the royals.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts are private ones, kept within.

clue.text: Hard work at the mill?

explanation.surface: Toiling at the flour mill.
explanation.definitionFit: Grind means tedious labour, and also crushing corn into flour as a mill does.

clue.text: Plant at the water-side lose no time!

explanation.surface: A command to hurry past the reeds on the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: A rush is a marsh plant by water, and to hurry is to waste no time.

clue.text: Polish dossier

explanation.surface: A file of papers from Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: To file is to smooth or polish with a tool, and a file is a folder of documents.

clue.text: Rider in the main backing recesses

indicators.note: in places the rider inside the other piece
backing means the word for the main is reversed

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
a rider is an addition to a document, like a postscript, PS

explanation.surface: A horseman retreats into hollows by the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old poetic term for the open sea; a rider added to a document is like a postscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Apses are vaulted semicircular alcoves at the end of a church.

clue.text: A reformer making men read-fancy!

indicators.note: fancy suggests the letters are arranged in a fanciful new way

explanation.surface: A reformer gets men to read fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' signals rearranging MEN READ.
explanation.definitionFit: An amender makes changes or corrections, so improves things.

clue.text: Tree maintenance

explanation.surface: Looking after trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The service tree is a European rowan relative, and servicing is upkeep of machines.

clue.text: Quite possibly male lit out forever

indicators.note: quite possibly hints the letters may come in another order
out suggests the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A man's reading is perhaps out of print for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite possibly' and 'out' both signal rearranging MALE LIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-time record holds for every period, so loosely for always.

clue.text: An evacuation soldiers handle

parts.note: RE, Royal Engineers, is a common crossword abbreviation for soldiers
to treat someone is to handle them

explanation.surface: Troops manage the clearing of an area.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a withdrawal of troops, an evacuation from a position.

clue.text: An animal sanctuary in decay

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: rot is decay
a den is a private retreat or sanctuary

explanation.surface: A creature lives in a crumbling refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in decay' reads as a description of the sanctuary, but decay supplies the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodent is a gnawing mammal such as a rat or mouse.

clue.text: Shut up in winter, naturally

indicators.note: in tells you the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: Of course people stay shut indoors in winter.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across WINTER and NATURALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern is to confine someone, such as an enemy alien in wartime.

clue.text: Land in the water

parts.note: a plain description of a patch of ground surrounded by sea

explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, ground surrounded by sea.

clue.text: Setting one against a certain work of art

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Setting one item against a particular painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setting' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a religious painting, especially in the Orthodox Church.

clue.text: Underworld team bearing with church feud

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself
a side is a team
N, north, is a compass bearing
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A team from hell fights the church.
explanation.walkthrough: CE, the Church of England, is the national church in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissidence is disagreement or dissent, a state of conflict.

clue.text: No matter how regarded, this is sound

indicators.note: this says the word reads the same from either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: However you look at it, this is a sound argument.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads the same forwards and backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A toot is a short blast on a horn, a noise.

clue.text: Staggering around Oriental court or returning to office again

indicators.note: around means the first piece wraps the others

parts.note: staggering means reeling
E, eastern, stands for Oriental

explanation.surface: A drunk stumbles round an Eastern palace, voted back in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staggering' looks like an adjective meaning astonishing, but it supplies the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-electing voters put a politician back into the same position.
